title: Artificial Intelligence
description: This course provides a broad, rigorous introduction to the core problems, algorithms, and models in artificial intelligence.  Students gain a thorough understanding of the organizing framework of intelligent agents, the algorithmic paradigm of search, logical and probablistic reasoning, logical and probabilistic planning and decision making, and an introduction to statistical machine learning.  After completing this course students will be well prepared for advanced specialized courses in artificial intelligence, and to begin research.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of search algorithms in AI.
Demonstrate understanding of logical and probabilistic reasoning.
Demonstrate understanding of decision making and machine learning.
Implement AI algorithms and models in an appropriate programming language.
required_materials: AIMA: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach, 4ed, by Stuart Russell and Peter Norvig, [https://aima.cs.berkeley.edu/](https://aima.cs.berkeley.edu/).  US or Global Edition
PMLAI: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction [https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)
recommended_materials: AICA: Artificial Intelligence: Foundations of Computational Agents, 3ed, by David Poole and Alan Mackworth, [https://artint.info/3e/html/ArtInt3e.html](https://artint.info/3e/html/ArtInt3e.html)
AIPP: Artificial Intelligence: Principles and Practice, by George Luger, [https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-57437-5](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-57437-5)
technology_requirements: Computer capable of accessing the internet and running compilers, interpreters, and text editors
